newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks sharply off in morning, properties hit.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks sharply off in morning, properties hit.

text.p: A slide in Hong Kong property counters dragged the territory's stocks sharply lower in Thursday morning trade, with the Hang Seng Index briefly falling below the 13,000 level.
The blue-chip index was down 87.79 points, or 0.67 percent, at 13,031.34 after tumbling to an early low of 12,981.28.
Turnover was HK$2.77 billion after the first hour of trade.
"People are still concerned about the property sector and interest rates," said Peter Lai, associate director at OCBC Securities.
Brokers said investors feared possible government intervention in the property market and a slump in prices following their sharp upward spiral.
Shares in Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd fell HK$0.55 to HK$71.25 and Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd fell HK$0.75 to HK$86.25.
Henderson Land Development Co Ltd was off HK$0.75 at HK$65.50 and New World Development Co Ltd fell HK$0.30 to HK$42.80.

"People are waiting to get a clearer picture on interest rates," said Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager at Nikko Securities. The U.S. Federal Reserve's policy-setting body is due to meet on March 25.
"I don't like the trend the market has been on. It is not healthy," added Rossiter.
As of Wednesday's close, the Hang Seng Index was down 218 points since the start of the week.
Lai said the index was likely to trade in a range of 12,800 to 13,200 points in the near term.
"There is no foreign inflow of funds. I think the market should be trading in a range," he said. "Below 12,800 points it is very attractive."
Shares in Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd fell HK$0.05 to HK$11.95 after rising to HK$12.10 earlier.
The Hong Kong flag carrier posted a 27.9 percent surge in 1996 net profit to HK$3.81 billion on Wednesday.

Shares in Shenzhen Expressway Co Ltd slipped HK$0.05 to HK$2.725 on their second day of trading. The share made its market debut on Wednesday and closed 26.14 percent higher at HK$2.775 compared with an issue price of HK$2.20.
HSBC Holdings Plc fell HK$2.00 to HK$189.00 but Hang Seng Bank Ltd rose HK$0.25 to HK$84.00.
March Hang Seng futures were down 105 points at 13,025.
